q1_progression.your_take: The author is dead right and the orchestrator's two-track split is the safe answer, not the correct one. A menu of 17 shifts at first launch is the single most Disco-betraying surface in the build: Disco's whole structural claim is that the world arrives at you, not that you shop the world. The fix isn't 'career mode plus practice library' — that's a Steam-store framing of a thing that should feel like a rota. The fix is: you have a rota. The rota shows your next shift and, peripherally, the shift after that. Completed shifts collapse into a portfolio (the e-portfolio gag writes itself for FRCEM candidates). Locked shifts are not greyed out menu items — they don't exist on the rota yet because the rota hasn't been published. Where I push back on the orchestrator: the Practice library should NOT survive as a co-equal second mode behind a 'study' door. That hedges the bet and tells the player 'the structure is decorative, here's the real menu'. Bin it as a launcher surface. Re-expose individual cases only as revisits inside the e-portfolio after you've worked them, plus a single 'random call' button for daily warm-up that pulls one already-completed shift.
q1_progression.specific_recommendation: Unlock rule: hybrid, narrative-weighted. Shifts are grouped into three blocks of roughly five shifts each, sequenced by clinical mileage (block 1 = bread-and-butter resus + minors that any CT1 should be safe with; block 2 = diagnostic-trap shifts and the start of the arcs; block 3 = the multi-case overnight nights and the legacy-payoff shifts). Block N+1 unlocks when you've passed the *previous block's keystone shift* at F2+ band (one keystone per block, not all five). Within a block, you can pick from currently-rota'd shifts but only 2-3 are visible at once — 'the rota goes up Friday'. Entry shift = a deliberately-easy day-shift minors+resus combo that establishes Aoife McGrath, the nurse-in-charge, and the e-portfolio loop. From the current catalogue: the chest-pain-in-the-waiting-room minors case is the right entry vibe but it's currently a single encounter — package it with the frequent-flyer intoxicated as a 'first day, minors floor' shift. Late-game / locked-until-block-3: Brennan SDH on apixaban (legacy/anticoag judgement requires you to have already seen a head-injury done right), the massive PE post-op (requires the player to have learnt to mistrust 'just anxiety'), aortic dissection (this one is *the* Disco-betrayal-trap and must come after the player has confidently anchored on STEMI once already in an earlier shift — it doesn't work as shift 1). Beth ectopic and Sarah hen-do anaphylaxis are mid-game arc shifts. Disorienting first shift: yes, but not Disco-amnesiac. The disorientation is procedural — you don't know where the gloves are, the nurse-in-charge is testing you, the consultant is on a coffee break, the e-portfolio is empty. Mechanical confusion, not narrative confusion. Practice library: deleted as a top-level mode; replaced by an in-fiction e-portfolio that only contains shifts you've worked, plus the 'random recall' single-case warm-up.

q2_titles.your_take: The author is right and the orchestrator's chief-complaint reframe is correct in shape but undersold in stakes. Right now the titles are the answer key printed above the question. 'Aortic dissection — Type A masquerading as inferior STEMI' tells the player exactly which trap to not fall into, which means the entire teaching point of that case — that it presents as a STEMI and you have to earn the dissection — is given away in the chrome. This is the single most expensive UX bug in the build measured against the Disco bar, because Disco's writing is *all about what you don't yet know*. Where I'd push the orchestrator's proposal further: chief-complaint-as-title is good, but the better Disco-equivalent is the orchestrator's own throwaway suggestion — 'Beth, 26F, hen-do' — *person, not problem, not even complaint*. The triage card is what the nurse-in-charge says to you, in her voice, in eight to twelve words. That's the title. The complaint is in the body of the triage note, not the header.
q2_titles.specific_recommendation: Title format: `<First name>, <age><sex>, <one-line vibe>` — e.g. 'Beth, 26F, brought in from a hen-do', 'Mr Brennan, 78M, fell off a ladder, on apixaban', 'Unknown male, ~40, brought in by police, smells of vodka'. No diagnosis word in the player-facing title, ever. Add a `clinical_title` field to the case YAML (populate with the current titles verbatim — this is one find-replace). Surface the clinical title in three places only: (1) the post-disposition debrief screen as 'What this was:'; (2) the e-portfolio / completed-shifts log; (3) the citations panel at debrief. NOT on the encounter header during play, NOT on the shift board, NOT on the rota. The debrief should show both side-by-side — 'How she came in: Beth, 26F, hen-do, throat closing. What this was: Anaphylaxis, adult, peanut cross-contamination.' That two-line reveal is the *learning moment*; it's currently being burned at t=0 instead of t=disposition. Ambient cases on the shift dashboard: same format, shorter — 'Cubicle 4: chest pain, 58M, sweaty' / 'Cubicle 7: vomiting, 22F, ?pregnant'. Diagnosis reveal: at debrief only. Not at working_dx commit (the player committing a wrong dx and then watching the case unfold is the highest-value teaching moment in the build — don't spoil it the moment they click). The committed working_dx is shown in the debrief alongside the actual diagnosis, with a tick or a soft 'no'. Three of the current 17 already half-conform ('Chest pain in the waiting room — minors' is closer); rewrite all 17 in one sitting so the voice stays consistent (Aoife McGrath's voice, or the triage nurse's voice — pick one and hold it).

q3_ed_vs_em.your_take: Author is right, fix is cheap, and the orchestrator has the scope correct. The only edge case worth flagging is self-identification in bedside dialogue: when McGrath or the player says 'I'm the ED reg' or a relative asks 'are you the ED doctor?', those become 'EM reg' / 'EM doctor' — but when a *patient* or *relative* says 'the ED' meaning the place ('we've been in the ED for six hours'), that's correct and stays. Also: 'ED nurse' is genuinely the standard UK usage for the role and should not be touched — nurses don't typically self-describe as 'EM nurse' the way doctors do. The player grade question matters: F1 in the ED is real but FRCEM SAQ content sits at CT1-CT3, so the player default should be EM CT1 / EM SHO, not F1, with F1 and F2 retained as selectable lower difficulty bands (you're playing as the F1 on the firm). The voice work is the bigger lift than the find-replace; budget an afternoon for McGrath's lines.
q3_ed_vs_em.specific_recommendation: Files to touch: (1) `src/state/consultant.ts:20` — `CONSULTANT_ROLE = 'EM consultant'`. (2) Grep the codebase and YAML for the strings: 'ED consultant', 'ED registrar', 'ED reg', 'ED SHO', 'ED doctor', 'ED trainee', 'ED clinician' — all become EM-prefixed. (3) Grep for 'ED nurse', 'ED nursing', 'nurse-in-charge of the ED' — LEAVE THESE. ED nurse is correct UK usage. (4) Grep for 'in ED' as a workplace-adjective shorthand ('I work in ED') — that's also fine, it means the department. (5) Default player role: re-tag to 'EM CT1' (default) with F1/F2 retained as easier difficulty framings ('you're shadowing as the F2 today'). (6) McGrath's bio comment at `consultant.ts:5` is already correct ('consultant in EM') — that's the reference voice, the code just drifted from its own spec. Edge cases: McGrath signing a memo or e-portfolio sign-off — she'd write 'EM Consultant, Skittstown General ED' (specialty, then place). Any in-game certificate, rota header, or trust email signature follows that pattern. The trust's department is still 'Emergency Department' on signage and on the rota header.

single_biggest_design_change_for_skitt: Q1, by a wide margin, and it isn't close. Q2 is the highest-leverage single edit per hour of work — rewriting 17 titles and adding one YAML field probably buys you the biggest visible Disco-bar jump for the smallest diff. But Q1 is the change that decides whether The Skitt is a study app with narrative skin or actually the thing it claims to be. The 17-shift menu is the load-bearing structural confession that this is currently a CME revision tool wearing a costume; replacing it with a rota-and-portfolio loop is what lets the Dwarf-Fortress sim bar (the shift as a living system with ambient cases, arcs that thread across shifts, the nurse-in-charge who remembers you) actually do its work, because right now the player can short-circuit every emergent property by just picking the case they want from a menu. Career-mode-with-a-rota is also what makes Q2's reveal-at-debrief land — a chief-complaint title only feels like a chief complaint if the case is what's in front of you tonight, not what you picked off a shelf. Fix Q1 and Q2 becomes load-bearing instead of cosmetic; fix Q2 without Q1 and you've made the menu prettier.
